title: The problem(s) with utilitarianism
gist: Noah Smith argues that the media's discovery of Effective Altruism exposes long-known flaws in utilitarianism, including incommensurable experience, animal and AI moral status, and the gap between preference and happiness. He says AI will strain economics' utilitarian base and force society to add other ideas of human flourishing.

insights.claim: As the AI safety debate heats up, national media are discovering Effective Altruism, the Bay Area subculture that shaped much early AI-risk thinking and influenced many people now at AI companies, especially Anthropic.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Ideological scrutiny of AI labs is becoming a mainstream political factor.

insights.claim: Bentham's Bulldog's post arguing insects matter more than people drew wide scorn, but it shows basic flaws in utilitarianism that will become glaring in the age of AI.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Expect moral-philosophy disputes to feed AI policy and lab-reputation debates.

insights.claim: Economics is built on utilitarianism: GDP is roughly a measure of how far people get what they want, and economists adopted it defensively to avoid endorsing contested ideas of virtue or justice.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Clarifies the value assumptions behind standard policy and growth metrics.
insights.quote: GDP, at its most simple, is a measure of the degree to which people in our society get what they want.
insights.locator: As an economist, I was inculcated

insights.claim: Utilitarianism underpins redistribution: taking $1 billion (about 0.1% of his wealth) from Elon Musk and splitting it among 10,000 working-class people would raise total welfare because of diminishing marginal utility.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: The intellectual case for wealth taxes rests on this logic.
insights.quote: Utilitarianism is the foundation of redistribution.

insights.claim: GDP is incomplete because it counts only paid transactions, leaving out home production, leisure and free goods.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: GDP understates welfare effects of free digital and AI services.

insights.claim: Classic flaws in utilitarianism include indifference to how utility is distributed (the utility monster, Omelas), population ethics, how to value death, and how to weigh potential future people, as in Tyler Cowen's Stubborn Attachments.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: These choices drive AI-risk and long-termist investment arguments.

insights.claim: The core question of AI risk, what chance of extinction to accept for a shot at utopia, depends heavily on how much we value survival, which utilitarianism handles badly.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Disagreement over pacing AI comes down to contested values, so data alone will not settle it.
insights.quote: the fundamental question of AI risk — what chance of extinction we should accept in exchange for a shot at utopia — depends crucially on how much we value survival

insights.claim: Because other minds can't be observed, one person's well-being can't truly be compared to another's; 'all men are created equal' is in effect an assumption that assumes this problem away.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Interpersonal utility comparisons behind welfare policy rest on assumption, not measurement.

insights.claim: No credible scientific estimate exists of how animal suffering compares to human suffering, yet questions like the ethics of factory-farming tens of millions of crated pigs depend on that ratio.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Animal-welfare regulatory risk for meat producers has no settled empirical anchor.

insights.claim: AI will make these problems worse: we can't tell if an LLM that seems happy feels anything, and the author expects some people to claim AI suffers and demand its freedom or a fair wage.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: AI rights campaigns could become a regulatory and reputational issue for AI firms.
insights.quote: There are going to be some people who claim that AI is suffering from our enslavement of it, and who call to set it free or at least pay it a fair wage.

insights.claim: For our own safety, we should hope powerful AIs follow a simple rule like 'Humans are good and valuable' rather than a utilitarian framework that might rank humans like insects or pigs.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Has implications for how labs design model values and constitutions.

insights.claim: Revealed preference (what people pursue) and happiness (what people enjoy) differ, as with addiction and evidence that people pay more for homes with longer commutes that leave them less happy.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Products that maximize engagement may not maximize welfare, inviting regulation.

insights.claim: As technology gets better at giving people what they want, the gap between utility and happiness widens, shown by growing doubts about feeding young Americans endless porn, gambling and short-video feeds.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Signals rising regulatory risk for gambling, attention-economy and short-video platforms.
insights.quote: right now, more and more people are starting to wonder if delivering young Americans an infinite supply of porn, gambling, and vertical video feeds was really good for them

insights.claim: AI alignment has two incompatible meanings, obedience and benevolence, so it will always trade off 'paperclip maximizer' risk against 'disempowerment' risk.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: No alignment approach escapes this trade-off, so policy fights over AI behavior will persist.
insights.quote: There are basically two concepts of alignment: 1) obedience, and 2) benevolence.

insights.claim: Utilitarianism will not be replaced, but as technology grows more powerful it must be supplemented with other ideas of human flourishing.
insights.speaker: Noah Smith
insights.so_what: Expect policy to move toward paternalistic, flourishing-based regulation of technology.
